proof_steps.content: Use continuous linear block projections on EuclideanSpace R (Bool × Fin d), their difference D, and f(z)=norm(D z)^2. Derive df(z)[v]=2 inner(D z,D v) and d²f(z)[v,w]=2 inner(D v,D w) using existing Mathlib derivative APIs.

For each particle separately, concatenate its X and Y state blocks but use the same Fin d coordinate family from B_i in both blocks. The noise columns are pairs of sqrt(2 lambda) P_j(X_i), sqrt(2 lambda) P_j(Y_i). No concatenated Brownian motion across particles is asserted.

Build the combined initialized drift rows and ProgressiveL2 noise integrands from the supplied coordinate equations. The initial coordinates are filtration-0 strongly measurable by strong progressivity. Continuous coefficient fields on finite-time × full C×C yield all finite-horizon bounds and drift integrability.

Apply the existing compact Euclidean Itô theorem on the compact image of S×S separately for every i and horizon. Existing row regularity and generator integrability yield the squared-chord pathwise balance and an actual zero-initial martingale. Project row continuity back to both sphere-valued paths.

For unit x,y, sum_j norm(P_j(x)-P_j(y))^2=2(1-inner(x,y)^2). With norm(x-y)^2=2(1-inner(x,y)), the radial drift plus shared-noise correction equals -2 lambda(d-3) norm(x-y)^2-lambda norm(x-y)^4. This is an equality, with no Jensen substitution.

Use all particle coordinates in Z=(X,Y) ∈ C×C for the continuous generator. Obtain almost-sure global paths from countably many positive horizons and finite coordinate intersections; this handles coefficient dependence on all configurations.

For each horizon, take the finite weighted sum of the actual per-particle martingale residuals. Martingale integrability and the set-integral equality between 0 and T give exact zero expectation. Derive finite-horizon time integrability from compact bounds and joint measurability; convert NNReal stopped-time integrals to ordinary real interval integrals.

Reuse the locally bounded weak marginal evolution theorem for the full compact state, obtaining the oriented two-time balance and absolute continuity. Almost-sure path continuity gives continuous marginal laws, and the existing compact moving-law integral theorem makes G continuous. Mathlib FTC then gives every positive-time derivative and the derivative within Ici 0 at zero.
Finite-sum and Bochner-integral linearity identify the compact observables exactly with D, L, R4 and G in the accepted signature. R4 remains the average of the actual fourth moments.
